tasks.short: Plan each session from the student's last work, prepare practice exercises at the right level, teach the session, mark the practice and note what to do next.

steps.what: Tutor plans the session from the student's last work
Tutor finds or writes practice exercises at the student's level

loop.input: The topic, the student's level and test date, and exercises from the tutor's own bank; no name or grades.
loop.output: Draft practice exercises with an answer key.
loop.check: Code recomputes numeric answers and rejects items without a key. The tutor reads every item before use: does it practise the planned topic at this student's level, is the wording clear; unclear items are dropped or rewritten.
loop.stop: Approved by the tutor, or after two redrafts the tutor writes the exercises.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed bank does not cover every topic at every level the students bring.

steps.what: Tutor provides private instruction to the student or small group to improve academic performance
Student answers the practice on the practice platform instead of on paper
Tutor marks the practice the student hands in
Tutor notes in the student record what to work on next

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts practice exercises with an answer key from the topic, level and the tutor's own bank, and the tutor reads every item. Closed answers are marked against the key on the practice platform ({LMS}), so the tutor only marks open work, and the tutor writes the session note as today; it is a first record and keeps its time. Teaching stays with the tutor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exercises were searched for or written per student, and all practice was marked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Lesson editors can rewrite material at another difficulty, and practice tools mark closed items.
tasks.still_hard: Drafted exercises can miss the student's level; the tutor must read each one.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a student's maths problem is really a reading problem.
tasks.altitude: The tutor reviews drafted exercises instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether drafted exercises suit group homework support.

evidence.claim: LessonUp's lesson editor rewrites text at another difficulty and pulls word lists with definitions.
Live AI suggestions to tutors raised topic mastery by 4 percentage points, 9 for lower-rated tutors, in a preregistered randomised trial with about 900 tutors.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes in education institutions is high-risk; this design does not grade with AI.

assumptions: Boundary: from the last work to the session note; reports to parents are outside.
Input contract: last work handed in by the student; exercise bank kept by the tutor; fallback is writing exercises by hand.

Teaching and the session note keep their full time. s2 keeps 50: the tutor picks, reads and fixes drafted items instead of writing them all. s4 keeps 40 for open work. The student answering on the platform (s3b) replaces answering on paper.
No student data go into the drafting step.
research_questions: How many drafted exercises does the tutor keep?

incremental.description: Tutor tags the exercise bank by topic and level.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the tutor still writes most exercises (s2 80) and much practice is handed in on paper (s4 70) (6.0); high: drafted items need light edits and practice is done on the platform (15.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Book places on the agency's sessions, attend training on tutoring techniques, read the shared materials, try new techniques with students and log training hours.

steps.what: Tutor e-mails the coordinator to book a place on a session
Tutor participates in training and development sessions on tutoring practices
Tutoring coordinator marks attendance for the session in the learning platform
Tutor looks for articles and clips that explain the new techniques
Tutor tries new techniques with students and notes what worked
Tutor keeps a list of training hours: in a spreadsheet today; after the change the platform counts marked attendance and the tutor checks it

tasks.design: The agency's learning platform ({LMS}) lets tutors enrol in sessions themselves, holds the articles and clips for each technique next to the session, and records attendance as training hours. Attending, trying techniques with students and reflecting stay with the tutor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Places were booked by e-mail, materials searched for afterwards and hours kept in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning platforms combine self-enrolment, materials per session and attendance records.
tasks.still_hard: A technique only sticks when tried with real students.
tasks.human_edge: Adapting a new questioning technique to a shy student.

reach.learn: Whether materials per session raise use of new techniques.

evidence.claim: Learning platforms combine self-enrolment, materials per session and attendance records.
A tutoring firm with a works council needs its consent for tools that can monitor tutors.

assumptions: Boundary: from booking a session to the training log; choosing the agency's programme is outside.
Input contract: session calendar and materials kept by the tutoring coordinator; fallback is e-mail and spreadsheet.

Attending, trying techniques and noting what worked keep their full time. Enrolling in the agency's own platform is an ordinary booking and needs no approval. The coordinator's attendance mark (s2b, share 1) is other-role time. s5 keeps 10 for checking the hours.
Attendance records show hours, not tutors' performance.
research_questions: Do tutors use the materials after sessions?

incremental.description: Tutor asks the coordinator to fix a missing attendance mark.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few sessions have materials attached, so the tutor still searches (s3 90) (9.2); high: each session has its materials (12.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather school reports and goals, meet student and parents to agree needs, write and send the tutoring plan, compile progress and review it with parents and teachers.

steps.what: Parents send the school report and test dates to the tutor
Tutor collects school reports and teacher comments by e-mail
Tutor meets the student and parents to determine student needs
Tutor writes the tutoring plan with goals and test dates
Tutor reads the final plan before it goes: goals and test dates match what was agreed, the approach is clear for parents, and it goes to this family
Tutor sends the plan to the parents: by e-mail today, by one release in the booking tool after the change
Tutor compiles attendance and marks from session notes
Tutor assesses student progress with parents and teachers by phone

tasks.design: Parents fill in an intake form in the booking tool ({OTHER}) with subjects, goals, test dates and the school report. A plan template fills the student's details, goals and test dates, and the tutor writes the approach; the tutor reads the final plan and sends it to the parents in one release. Attendance and marks from the session register build a progress overview. Meetings and progress talks stay with the tutor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports and goals came in scattered e-mails, plans were written from scratch and progress compiled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking tools hold intake forms, registers and attendance reports.
tasks.still_hard: Parents and teachers see the student differently; the tutor has to reconcile them.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing in the intake that the real goal is confidence, not a grade.

reach.learn: Whether a shared intake form improves referrals.

evidence.claim: Momoyoga combines schedules, online booking and payment, attendance reports and messaging.
Tutors hold minors' grades and support needs; parents must be informed and data kept to a minimum.

assumptions: Boundary: from intake to agreed progress; ending the tutoring is outside.
Input contract: intake form filled in by parents; school report shared by parents; fallback is e-mail.

Meetings and progress talks keep their full time. s3 keeps 75: the template fills details, goals and dates, but the tutor writes the approach. s5 keeps 10 for checking the overview against missed sessions.
Parents' time is priced as customer time; teachers' time is outside the tutor's savings.
research_questions: Are plans sent sooner after intake?

incremental.description: Tutor follows up parents who skip the form.
Parents fill in the intake form and upload the school report themselves (work moved from the tutor's collecting).

approvals.approved_version: The tutoring plan with goals, test dates and approach exactly as checked by the tutor in s3b, sent once to this student's parents through the booking tool; any change needs a new check before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of parents skip the form, so the tutor still collects reports by e-mail (s1 70) (22.2); high: most parents use the form (27.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Help students during class or lab work, check who is stuck, monitor performance and note who needs extra help, set follow-up practice and tell the class teacher.

steps.what: Tutor assists students in classrooms, laboratories or computing centers
Students do the class practice on the practice platform instead of paper worksheets
Tutor checks each student's worksheet to see who is stuck
Tutor monitors student performance and notes who needs extra help
Tutor sets follow-up practice for students who need it
Tutor writes the concerns for the class teacher: by e-mail today; in the platform after the change, with the scores attached instead of copied
Tutor reads the note before sending: each concern matches what the tutor saw and the scores, and it goes to this class's teacher
Tutor sends the checked note to the class teacher in the platform

tasks.design: Students do class practice on the school's practice platform ({LMS}), which marks closed items against a key and shows the tutor which students are stuck on which item, so fewer rounds of the room are needed to find them. A list of students below a set score is the starting point for the tutor's help list; the tutor assigns follow-up practice from the bank and shares concerns with the teacher in the platform. Helping students stays in person; no AI judges learning.
tasks.previous_blocker: The tutor walked round checking worksheets and kept notes on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice platforms mark closed items and show progress per student live.
tasks.still_hard: A student who is stuck but quiet may not show it on screen.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing frustration before a student gives up.
tasks.altitude: The tutor goes to stuck students directly instead of looking for them.

reach.learn: Whether live views change how teachers group students.

evidence.claim: Practice platforms mark closed items against a key and show progress per student live.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes in education institutions is high-risk from 2 December 2027; this design uses fixed keys only.

assumptions: Boundary: from class work to the teacher informed; grading is outside.
Input contract: practice items and keys chosen by the class teacher; score threshold set by the tutor; fallback is paper worksheets.

Helping students keeps its full time. s3 keeps 60: the below-score list replaces collecting scores, but deciding who needs help stays. Writing concerns is a first record and keeps 90; only copying scores goes. Students practising on the platform (s1b) replaces paper worksheets.
Teachers' time is outside the tutor's savings.
research_questions: Do stuck students get help sooner?

already_counted.description: Tutor reads the live progress view.

incremental.description: Tutor sets up classes on the platform.

approvals.approved_version: The note with each named student's concern and scores exactly as checked by the tutor in s5b, sent once to this class's teacher in the practice platform; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half the practice stays on paper worksheets (s2 75, s3 80) (11.9); high: class practice runs on the platform (19.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The tutor keeps teaching, intake talks and judging progress; writing exercises, marking closed work and compiling notes shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A tutor who spends saved time on the students who struggle most.
